ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure gives the broken-line graph of the function f. It can be seen that the graph of f passes through the point (0,3), rises to the point (3,6), and then follows a descending line segment to the point (6,0). Near x=4, the graph is located on the descending line segment from (3,6) to (6,0). Reasoning: The slope of this descending line segment is f'(4) = (0 - 6) / (6 - 3) = -6/3 = -2. Because x=4 is on this line segment, f(4)=4 can be read from the straight line. Given h(x) = (x+1)f(x), using the product rule gives h'(x)=f(x)+(x+1)f'(x). Substitute x=4: h'(4)=f(4)+5f'(4)=4+5(-2)=4-10=-6.
